site.title: Asahi Suenaga
site.description: I build intuitive open-source software at Michigan State University while studying computer science. I have a sharp eye for detail and I look for perfection in executing my ideas.

bio-first: I study computer science and write good, clean code.
bio:
I believe there’s something irresistible about that instant when code compiles and abstract logic becomes real. But building isn't enough on its own; it has to be designed to actually work for people. 

That is why great software starts long before writing code. Every choice must feel intentional and frictionless. By combining thoughtful design with practical engineering, I turn user needs into clean, reliable systems. 

That intersection is where I operate. From initial concept to polished build, I craft software where design and code reinforce each other.

now.title: Now
now.text: Most of my time goes into earning a bachelor's degree in computer science at Michigan State University. I also co-lead finance and corporate relations at SpartaHack, MSU's official hackathon, and serve as secretary for the Japanese Student Association.
